title: Japan's Summer Plans Change as Costs Rise
paragraphs: Summer is a very popular time for travel in Japan. But this year, rising prices are changing many people's summer plans.
In June 2026, the research company Intage did an online survey of 5,000 people in Japan aged 15 to 79. It asked them about their plans for the summer holidays, from July 18 to September 30.

The survey found that the average summer holiday budget was 58,902 yen. This was 1,618 yen more than last year. It was the first increase in three years. But this does not mean that people are traveling more. In fact, 45.7% of people said their budget was higher because of high prices and a weak yen.

The most common plan for the summer was staying at home. In the survey, 38.6% of people chose this answer. Only 18.3% planned to travel in Japan and stay overnight, and 17.3% planned to eat out and go shopping.

Other things also changed people's plans. For example, 26.2% said the situation in Iran affected their plans. Some people spent less money or decided not to travel abroad. In addition, 18.1% said that bear sightings in different parts of Japan affected their plans. Some people changed where they would go in Japan or canceled outdoor activities.
Emiko Mori, an expert at Intage, said that high prices are strongly affecting many people's holiday plans this year.

Other research found similar results. The travel company JTB expected the number of Japanese people traveling in Japan in summer to fall by 4.4%. It also expected the number of people traveling abroad to fall by 8.8%. According to JTB, high costs are making people choose closer destinations instead of faraway places such as North America and Australia.
